biw_news.title: Robotic Dry Fiber Cell and 2,400-Ton Composite Press Cut Aerostructure Production Time by 90%
biw_news.summary: The COMPASS facility's advanced robotic dry fiber cell and high-tonnage composite press demonstrate high-rate manufacturing methods. This process drastically reduces build times for advanced structural carbon fiber components, with direct implications for automotive composite adoption.

biw_news.title: Thick Thermoplastic Composite Wing Ribs Advance Direct Stamping and Infusion Techniques
biw_news.summary: Daher's thermoplastic wing rib program validates patented direct stamping and infrared welding processes. These manufacturing innovations create highly loaded structures with optimized weight-to-strength ratios applicable to next-gen vehicle architecture.

biw_news.title: Tesla Roadster Patent Details Two-Piece Active Rear Wing and Crash-Safety Geometry
biw_news.summary: A newly published patent outlines an active two-piece aerodynamic wing engineered to shift between low-drag, high downforce, and dedicated crash-safety configurations. The mechanism highlights integration between vehicle body aerodynamics and structural crashworthiness management.

biw_news.title: Architected AFP Multifunctional Conductive Layers Replace Traditional Lightning Protection
biw_news.summary: Automated Fiber Placement (AFP) enables tailored conductive layers within composite materials, replacing single sheets of metallic protection. This engineering approach maintains structural integrity and electrical connectivity while reducing parasitic mass.

biw_news.title: Alpine Previews Next-Gen Electric Sports Car Architecture with Full-Scale Composite Veil Sculpture
biw_news.summary: Alpine has showcased its upcoming dedicated electric sports car platform (APP) through a detailed design sculpture. The underlying chassis and body architecture are engineered to support a lightweight mid-engine inspired EV layout.

biw_news.title: CFRP and Graphite Heat Dissipation Structures Achieve 47 Percent Mass Reduction
biw_news.summary: A collaborative development demonstrates carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) and graphite thermal devices matching aluminum's thermal conductivity. The resulting structural components drop weight significantly, showcasing advanced material substitution for demanding thermal-structural environments.
